newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwaiti to build a World Trade Center at home.
newsitem.headline: Kuwaiti to build a World Trade Center at home.

text.p: Kuwaiti businessman Ghazi al- Saqabi has secured a licence to build a World Trade Center in Kuwait, a project possibly worth up to $100 million.
Saqabi told Reuters on Monday the building would include a shopping mall, a hotel, office space and other facilities.
"I now have the license from the World Trade Centers Association Inc in the U.S. and the approval from the State of Kuwait" to go ahead with the project, he added.

Saqabi, who showed the official documents giving him the go-ahead, owns a group of firms involved in financial investment, real estate, construction and other functions in several Middle Eastern countries.

Saqabi plans to take partners in the World Trade Center project, but he said that would depend on the cost of acquiring land. The project cost could be halved if the state offered the land at a nominal price or according to a soft, long-term leasing accord.
"Tenders for construction will be offered. My company will compete with others for the contract," he said. "May the best offer win."
In neighouring United Arab Emirates (UAE), Dubai has a World Trade Center and another two are under construction in the emirates of Abu Dhabi and Sharjah.
Saqabi said he was considering similar projects in the UAE emirates of Ajman, Fujairah and Ras al-Khaimah.
